notes.title: Hades' Star 2025.1 is now available!
notes.content:
This major update focuses on changes requested by the community. To vote on future update features, join our Discord server: https://discord.gg/hadesstar

Detailed changelog: 

[list]
[*]Named Ship Loadouts allow saving module configurations and quickly refitting other ships, or constructing new identical ships. Access from the Module Installation page. (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1206751668344197191/threads/1274969769434419201)
[*]Leap and Dispatch now show visual indicator for the AOE damage radius at the landing site (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1206751668344197191/threads/1316265870846201888)
[*]A cancelled Dark Red Star search no longer resets the daily rich artifact timer (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1197268069370835114/threads/1298728480250396732)
[*]Flagship modules now persist their cooldowns across jumps, same as all other regular ship modules (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1197268069370835114/threads/1227370049388417064)
[*]Blast Drone now persists number of activations remaining between jumps to the White Star
[*]Fixed issue that could cause scheduled orders to link to/from a Chain Ray Drone weapon to fail to execute (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1197268069370835114/threads/1197492350222610462)
[*] Artifacts or Relics that are in the process of loading on the Transport ship will now always return to the planet if the Transport ship is destroyed, regardless of star type. This also fixes a bug where the Time Machine would show incorrect information when such a Transport is destroyed. (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1197268069370835114/threads/1206543942640865330)
[*] Remote Mining will now restart after using Artifact Boost (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1197268069370835114/threads/1288975052657791087)
[*] Fixed wrong background scaling in module buttons that have reduced width (https://discord.com/channels/255083954036670464/1326424577600917514)
[*] Corporation officers can now add a Discord webhook on the Corporation's settings, to receive notifications of events (ask your Corporation leader or see our Discord server for more information)
[*] Sector highlight for placing stations and setting miner routes changed to more subtle blue color
Corporation information window now shows the level of both Corporation flagships
[*] Leap, Dispatch, Vengeance, Destiny AOE indicators will now be colored same as the color of the ship activating the module
[*] Players can now register to the Mailing list from inside the game, and filter the email types they get
Weekly events will start at a fixed time. Upcoming events are visible through the new Events browser (accessible in the Leaderboards window).  
[*] New monthly White Star event offers 5x Corporation XP for all White Stars that are discovered while the event is active. The first event will start on April 14.

[/list]

notes.title: Hades' Star: DARK NEBULA is coming soon to Steam and Steam Deck!
notes.content:
Over the past 2 years, we've been hard at work strengthening the foundation of Hades' Star, so that the game can remain popular and viable for many more years in the future. The result of this effort is called Hades' Star: DARK NEBULA, a massive update to the game that is coming soon to Steam.

There are multiple posts at blog.hadesstar.com, describing the motivations, design goals and development process that went on during these years to give the update its final shape. You can review those if you want to dig deeper. However, most players will want to see how their daily gameplay will change, and what to do to keep progressing in the game at an optimal rate. For that purpose, we've prepared the following upgrade guide: 

[url=http://blog.hadesstar.com/2023/10/dark-nebula-upgrade-guide.html]http://blog.hadesstar.com/2023/10/dark-nebula-upgrade-guide.html[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33944744/172dbe7cec955762ca99009ccf32884ff600395b.png[/img]

[h1]Hades' Star: DARK NEBULA on Steam Deck[/h1]

The Steam Deck is a wonderful device that is perfect for games like Hades' Star. We have experimented a lot with it, and have created a completely new version of the game to suit the hardware. We found early on that the Steam Deck does not offer a great touch experience, so instead we've focused on a gamepad-exclusive interface. We can't wait to show you soon how well the game works on the device. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33944744/366380bedb5d2878bc26fb0c5020857b0c324c1e.jpg[/img]

Hades' Star: DARK NEBULA is currently scheduled for release on October 30, as an update to the current Hades' Star game on PC and Mac. Unforeseen issues may push this date back. The custom, Linux-native Steam Deck build will launch along with this update, and we aim to have it verified as fully compatible at launch or shortly after.
 
Thank you for supporting Hades' Star, and hope to see you in game!

notes.title: Private Red Star Season 5
notes.content:
Private Red Stars are a great way to get fellow Corporation members to help you out and maximize your Artifact collection. Now is a great time to start looking for a good Corporation whose members work well together and play Red Stars cooperatively.

On November 25, the 5th private Red Star season event begins. During the event, all private Red Stars will award event points to your Corporation, according to the star level, number of artifacts retrieved and Cerberus ships destroyed.

The event lasts a week. At the end, the top 200 Corporations (over 5,000 players) will receive Crystal rewards.

To see the event countdown timer, and for exact rewards information, open the Leaderboards window in game, select Top Corporations, then press the Red Star button.

Having trouble finding the perfect Corporation? Join our discord server (link below). There's a dedicated channel where the best Corporations advertise - or you can describe your play style and let the best Corporation contact you instead.

Hades' Star Official Discord Server: [url=https://discord.gg/hadesstar]https://discord.gg/hadesstar[/url]

notes.content:
Supergiant Games' early access roguelike Hades has had its next major update, which includes a final battle at the Gateway to the Underworld.

notes.title: Hades and the texture of the world
notes.content:
Hades is the latest game from Supergiant, a studio that sometimes seems to rival Klei Games in terms of classiness and poise and sheer polish. Hades is all about ancient gods smashing things up in the underworld. It's a Roguelite in which you fight your way through a shifting maze of classical horrors again and again and again. There is so much that's good about it I'm aiming to write something more comprehensive next week. For now, though, I wanted to talk about something I probably don't think about enough in games: the texture of the in-game world.

This is mythology, right, so it's all ancient temples and grandeur. What makes Supergiant's spin so memorable, though, is that the art really delivers a sense of what this world is like to touch. And what it's like to touch is slightly surprising. Everything around you in Hades is made of stone, but it's stone that seems to shatter like glass. It's glossy and heavy, but it's also fragile. It splinters and explodes as you barrel your way through the world, giving everyone you encounter a bit of a shoeing. Are you powerful, or is the world flimsy?

Glossy, polished, angular stone. This gives Hades a good deal of its character, I think. What a strange, lurid, heavy crystalline world this is. And it's all in service to the theme. Gods are weird in Hades, as they are in a lot of mythology. They're skittish and decadent and childish and unpredictable, and they like lavish temples of smooth reflective surfaces. And the whole thing's a bit precarious, too. These creatures fight all the time and fall out and smash each other in, and so their world has retained some of that depraved delicacy.

notes.title: How Hades brings Greek mythology into the modern day
notes.content:
Supergiant's Hades is in many ways a departure from the studio's earlier work. Unlike Bastion, Transistor, or Pyre, it's a roguelike dungeon crawler, and it's also the first of the team's games to be put out in early access.

One thing that ties all of Supergiant's work together, though, is a strong narrative. Hades' protagonist is Zagreus, a blurry member of the Greek pantheon who is seen only through fragmentary texts that identify him as the son of Hades, lord of the underworld. (He may have later been merged with the myth of the god of wine, Dionysus, further obscuring his original tales.) The developers took this loose foundation and built up their own character, a rebellious young man who wants to escape his father's underworld, tasking the player with battling through an ever-shifting maze of enemies in an attempt to reach the surface.

Creative director Greg Kasavin has worked on writing and implementing the narrative on all four of Supergiant's games, but this is the first one to draw on an existing mythology. He tells me that this narrative foundation first came from the structure of the game they wanted to make.

notes.title: Our Story So Far
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33944744/9a3415ab303e52faeec3aa1bd37e16f88fcb65ad.jpg[/img]

As a young college student, I spent countless hours playing Master of Orion. Now that I'm older, I'm finding [url=https://www.gamasutra.com/blogs/AndreasPapathanasis/20150427/241990/The_Time_problem.php]I no longer have the continuous time required to play and enjoy it.[/url]

Hades' Star is my attempt to capture some of [url=https://www.gamasutra.com/blogs/AndreasPapathanasis/20150715/248581/Improving_on_the_promise_of_Master_of_Orion.php]the promise of Master of Orion,[/url]
in a way that's compatible with my current time limitations. In Hades' Star, instead of starting a new game every time, you continue building on your previous progress - regardless if you last played 30 minutes ago or months ago. Instead of requiring hours to enjoy a session, most missions last from 5 to 20 minutes. If something happens and you have to go away from the game, your ships will carry out your orders in the meantime. Depth comes naturally over time as you progress your Empire, not by requiring you to navigate extreme complexity up front.

At the core of the game's design are [url=http://blog.hadesstar.com/2016/08/the-three-design-pillars-of-hades-star.html]our three core pillars[/url]: 
[list]
[*] Progression and Exploration
[*] Strategic Depth
[*] Social Diplomacy
[/list]
Every decision we make on how to evolve the game can be traced back to one or more of these pillars.

Hades' Star is not a game for everyone - more so than the average game. If you are looking for an immersive space game that you can play for hours on end, or a single player game, you won't find it here. But if, like me, you enjoy building a massive space Empire over time, a little bit at a time, and participate in exciting missions with other players, you should definitely give it a try. 

Hades' Star is a free to play game, supported by in app purchases a small percentage of our players choose to make. All content is available for free to all players over time, and we guarantee it will always stay that way.  [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/HadesStar/comments/5hpcst/question_for_he_devs/db30mk6/] See this post[/url] for why we  believe this is the best choice for the game. 

Since we launched the game almost 2 years ago, we've been lucky to have a growing, passionate community. We have evolved the game significantly with new gameplay, star types and content, over more than 12 major updates. We hope our Steam launch builds on that momentum and allows us to improve the game for many years to come. 

I hope to see you around in the Hades galaxy. 

- Andreas
